annotation.summary_en: Qualitative co-design and interaction study with young adults using a design justice approach to identify ethical considerations when a humanoid social robot serves as the interface for an LLM. It maps considerations across four dimensions: interaction, co-design, terms of service and relationship.
key_provisions_or_claims: LLM-based social robots risk misinformation, emotional disruption, dependence and bias, possibly amplified by physical embodiment.
Ethical considerations are mapped across four dimensions: interaction, co-design, terms of service, relationship.
Participants raised concerns about gender, race and stereotypes in robot design choices.
Design justice methodology is evaluated as an empirical approach for LLM-based social robotics.
Users should have a say in design, including terms of service.
annotation.title_clean: An Empirical Design Justice Approach to Identifying Ethical Considerations in the Intersection of Large Language Models and Social Robotics
annotation.title_en: An Empirical Design Justice Approach to Identifying Ethical Considerations in the Intersection of Large Language Models and Social Robotics
